admission.justification: Keeping heavy operation imports and optional dashboard supervision out of discovery prevents a harness from abandoning a valid tool server before it can advertise its tools, while retaining boot-time caller identity prevents later task state from being mislabeled as the launch.

applicability: The ordinary or launch-bound explainer MCP serving process: its canonical declarations, lazy operation collaborators, light boot-time caller writer and shared post-discovery start. The outside-scratch sweep child is the explicitly separate execution site for the heavy worktree owner.
conditions: Tool declarations retain canonical schema models and operation validation.
The service supplier is explicit; reset clears the bound instance and pending supplier.
The produced tools/list answer schedules start_after_discovery on the event loop; call_tool reaches that same once-per-process latch before dispatch if a client never lists.

The first latch attempt is consumed even with no config: the outside-scratch reconciliation launcher is reached, while dashboard autostart requires a config and respects dashboard.autoStart. Later lists or calls start neither again.

The sweep thread invokes a one-shot child through the same Python executable with stdin=DEVNULL, captured output and a 600-second timeout; the heavy worktree import occurs only in the child. Thread-launch/child/sweep failures are contained and logged; dashboard-launch failure is contained.
exclusions: A guarantee that serialized tools/list bytes reached the client before the scheduled callback.
A blanket claim that every optional startup collaborator is deferred, or that the whole product imports no worktree code in any process.
An any-load five-second promise, real installed-host/sweep-result proof, or review/acceptance.
The existing autoStart=true dashboard test is not credited with proving no-config or autoStart=false branches.

statement: Registration declares canonical light models and loads operation payloads on invocation, while worktree services and token measurement initialize only at their first dependent operation; the light tool-event writer stays at startup to capture boot-time caller identity. After producing a tools/list answer, the server schedules one shared post-discovery start with loop.call_soon; a first tool call uses that same latch as the fallback for clients that never list. Initialization starts neither the outside-scratch sweep nor dashboard supervision. The joint start attempts the sweep even without a config, and invokes dashboard autostart only with a config and its setting; the heavy worktree sweep runs in a one-shot child with no access to MCP stdin rather than importing its owner into the serving process.
